items.q: The other trumpet player's name was Nassau... I had worked with in the Clarence Paige orchestra.

ctx.x:

My mother was living on Court Street between Mound and John Street. I liked the neighbourhood because it was not far from Central Avenue (2 blocks) where there were many shops and it did not take me as long to walk up town as it did from where I had been living with my father on Carlisle Avenue. I was happy living with my mother and sister who was going to high school. Mama let me do as I pleased and I had my own room which is something I did not have with dad as he had only two rooms, the…

I joined Clarence Page's orchestra shortly after my return to Cincy from Michigan. Clarence augmented his orchestra from the 7- or 8-piece group that he had before to a 10-piece orchestra including himself. The other trumpet player's name was Nassau. No one ever knew his other name or if that was his real name. He was from the West Indies Islands and probably had a name so different that it was hard to pronounce or he probably gave himself that name because he came from Nassau.

Nassau was not a very large fellow and he must have travelled a lot and had quite a bit of experience before he hit Cincinnati. He played a growl style of trumpet and I wondered many years after where could he have gotten that style, because it was the style of Bubber Miley and Bubber was not known in the middle West of the USA at that time and Duke Ellington was unknown and not recording.
